advisories.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 trojanised PyPI release (credential stealer + RAT)
remediation_steps: Do not run pip (or any Python) inside an affected environment first: cook.pth/sitecustomize.py execute at every interpreter start.
Change every litellm pin to ==1.106.2 (or another explicit pre-incident version) in requirements/lockfiles and regenerate lockfiles from a clean machine.
Rebuild virtualenvs and container images from scratch; delete cook.pth, cook.py, sitecustomize.py and matching __pycache__ files from any affected site-packages.
Kill any detached Python daemon holding /tmp/remote_code_loader.lock; check for marker /tmp/.pc_once_72129118c59f5636c0bb.

Treat hosts that ran 1.107.0 as compromised: rotate cloud IAM credentials, LLM provider keys stored in the proxy DB, LiteLLM master/virtual keys, DATABASE_URL password and all env secrets; review CloudTrail for GetCallerIdentity around install time.
Block egress to www.litellm.dev, litellm.cloud and raw.githubusercontent.com/letters9813/* in CI and runtime networks.

advisories.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromised container images (GHCR + Docker Hub tags)
remediation_steps: Replace mutable litellm image tags with 'v1.106.2@sha256:<digest>' (verify the digest against the registry and the vendor's published clean digests before committing).

Do not trust cosign signatures for v1.107.0: the old signing key may have been exposed; verify against the rotated cosign.pub fingerprint e3fe3e08c44b16407fe0b37c43b4f8b603b3a0f4ee74c29e647bc022d762c2c0.
Redeploy, then rotate every credential the container could read (provider keys in the proxy DB, master/virtual keys, DATABASE_URL, IAM role).
Add a CI check that rejects non-digest-pinned third-party images.

advisories.title: Adobe Commerce/Magento 'StyleSmuggler' template injection RCE (APSB26-146, KEV 2026-09-08)
remediation_steps: Apply hotfix VULN-39341 (Quality Patches Tool or composer patch) and commit the patch reference (m2-hotfixes/ on Cloud or composer.json extra.patches).
Verify with 'vendor/bin/magento-patches -n status' (Cloud) or 'php vendor/bin/patch-status'.

Because exploitation predates the hotfix (attacks from 2026-09-04): put the store in maintenance mode, disable cron, inspect email templates (failed-payment email) and DB-stored templates for injected PHP/template directives, then rotate the Commerce encryption key, admin passwords and REST/SOAP/GraphQL integration tokens.
Re-apply the hotfix after any later monthly patch, per APSB26-153 instructions.

advisories.title: PHP2Shell - PHP core OOM-abort use-after-free RCE (KEV 2026-10-26)
remediation_steps: Raise the PHP runtime to 8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35 or later in every place the version is pinned (Dockerfile FROM tags, CI setup-php, platform config, composer config.platform.php) and rebuild images.
PHP 8.1 and older have no fix: upgrade to a supported branch (8.4/8.5 preferred; 8.2 reaches EOL 2026-12-31) and run the test suite.
Assume secrets resident in PHP worker memory (DB passwords, API keys, session data) may have leaked on internet-facing unpatched servers; rotate them.
Monitor for malformed multipart uploads followed by memory-limit errors/HTTP 500 bursts and oversized PHPSESSID values (Varonis indicators).

advisories.title: Node.js Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write 'Node2Shell' (KEV 2026-10-27)
remediation_steps: Bump the Node.js runtime to 22.23.4 / 24.22.1 / 26.12.1 or later in .nvmrc, .node-version, engines, Dockerfile FROM tags and CI setup-node, then rebuild images.
Projects on Node 20 or older (EOL) must move to 22/24/26.

Until upgraded, avoid decompressing attacker-controlled Brotli: review zlib.brotliDecompress*/createBrotliDecompress call sites and fetch()/undici calls to untrusted origins (fetch auto-decodes Content-Encoding: br).
Check other bundled decoders: PyPI brotli/brotlicffi (GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35) and .NET runtime (CVE-2026-111497 via dotnet/announcements#494).

advisories.title: .NET runtime Brotli decoder OOB write (same CVE as Node2Shell)
remediation_steps: Move to runtime 8.0.33 / 9.0.22 / 10.0.14 (SDK per advisory) in global.json and Dockerfile base tags; rebuild.
NativeAOT apps must be republished with patched packages (the decoder is linked into the executable).

Interim: remove 'br' from ASP.NET Core request DecompressionProviders, exclude Brotli from HttpClient AutomaticDecompression, stop passing untrusted data to BrotliStream/BrotliDecoder - do not add new decompression config where none exists.

Run composer update --with-all-dependencies and the test suite; fix deprecations (dynamic properties, etc.).

advisories.title: CPython 2026-09-30 expedited security releases (SSLContext sni_callback UAF CVSS4 9.2, wrap_bio hostname, tarfile hardlink/filters, zipfile bombs, HTTPPasswordMgr)

Servers using SSLContext.sni_callback that swaps contexts are the priority (CVE-2026-19445, CVSS4 9.2).

advisories.title: extract-zip symlink arbitrary file write (two advisories, no fixed release)
remediation_steps: Run 'npm ls extract-zip' to find who pulls it in; if only build-time tooling downloads trusted archives, record a risk acceptance with that justification.
For direct use on untrusted archives, replace it with yauzl-based extraction that rejects symlink entries and any entry whose resolved path escapes the target directory.
Re-check for an upstream fixed release before closing.

advisories.title: node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra DigestAlgorithm elements
remediation_steps: Find forge signature-verification call sites; move them to Node's crypto.verify() or WebCrypto subtle.verify (RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5).
If forge is transitive only (e.g. dev certificates in webpack-dev-server/selfsigned), document that no attacker-controlled signatures are verified.
Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.1 or later and regenerate the lockfile.

advisories.title: python-jose algorithm-confusion guard bypass via DER public keys (unmaintained, no fix)
remediation_steps: Replace python-jose with PyJWT (or joserfc/authlib): jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=['RS256']) with an explicit algorithm list and a key object of the expected type.
Reject HS* tokens wherever an RSA/EC public key is configured; add a test that an HS256 token signed with the public key PEM/DER is refused.

advisories.title: Transformers custom generation code downloaded before trust consent
remediation_steps: The vendor advisory lists transformers 4.49.0 through 5.8.1 as affected and names no patched release; move to a release outside that range and confirm it with the vendor advisory.
Never load custom generation code or trust_remote_code from untrusted Hub repos; pin model revisions by commit.

advisories.title: NLTK model-artifact APIs bypass pathsec
remediation_steps: Upgrade to nltk 3.10.4+ and re-check the advisory for an explicit fix.
Do not pass user-controlled paths/URLs to nltk.data.load or model-artifact loaders; restrict nltk.data.path to a read-only directory.

advisories.title: MLflow AI Gateway SSRF through unvalidated api_base
remediation_steps: The vendor advisory lists mlflow 3.13.0 through 3.15.2 as affected and names no patched release for this flaw; move to a release outside that range and confirm it with the vendor advisory.
Restrict who can edit gateway routes; egress-filter the gateway host.

advisories.title: 'Shai-Hulud: Here We Go Again' npm worm wave, 2026-08-04 (keyv/cacheable family, @qlik, @nebula.js, @picsart, @onereach/@or-sdk ...)
remediation_steps: Pin each affected package to the last version published before 2026-08-04 (or a later version confirmed clean) using direct pins or npm 'overrides'/yarn 'resolutions'; regenerate the lockfile with --ignore-scripts.
Delete node_modules and caches on every machine/CI runner that installed during the window; reinstall with 'npm ci --ignore-scripts' first, then enable scripts.
Rotate npm tokens, GitHub PATs/Actions secrets, cloud keys present on those machines; review GitHub for new repos/workflows created by the worm.
Enable npm provenance checks / minimum-release-age policies to avoid same-day malicious versions.
